column291: A type of single address space multiprocessor in which some memory accesses are much faster than others depending on which processor asks for which word.
column292: The process of coordinating the behavior of two or more processes, which may be running on different processors.
column293: A synchronization device that allows access to data to only one processor at a time.
column294: A function that processes a data structure and returns a single value.
column295: An API for shared memory multiprocessing in C, C++, or Fortran that runs on UNIX and Microsoft platforms. It includes compiler directives, a library, and runtime directives.
column296: Communicating between multiple processors by explicitly sending and receiving information.
column297: A routine used by a processor in machines with private memories to pass a message to another processor.
column298: A routine used by a processor in machines with private memories to accept a message from another processor.
column299: Collections of computers connected via I/O over standard network switches to form a message-passing multiprocessor.
column300: Rather than selling software that is installed and run on customers' own computers, software is run at a remote site and made available over the Internet typically via a Web interface to customers. SaaS customers are charged based on use versus on ownership.
column301: Informally, the peak transfer rate of a network; can refer to the speed of a single link or the collective transfer rate of all links in the network.
column302: The bandwidth between two equal parts of a multiprocessor. This measure is for a worst case split of the multiprocessor.
column303: A network that connects processor-memory nodes by supplying a dedicated communication link between every node.
column304: A network that supplies a small switch at each node.
column305: A network that allows any node to communicate with any other node in one pass through the network.
column306: An I/O scheme in which portions of the address space are assigned to I/O devices, and reads and writes to those addresses are interpreted as commands to the I/O device.
column307: A mechanism that provides a device controller with the ability to transfer data directly to or from the memory without involving the processor.
column308: An I/O scheme that employs interrupts to indicate to the processor that an I/O device needs attention.
column309: A program that controls an I/O device that is attached to the computer.
column310: The process of periodically checking the status of an I/O device to determine the need to service the device.
column311: A UNIX API for creating and manipulating threads. It is structured as a library.
column312: The ratio of floating-point operations in a program to the number of data bytes accessed by a program from main memory.
